properties.areaDesc: Hatcher Pass; Western Susitna Valley; Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley; Northern Susitna Valley
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 26 at 3:50PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Yentna and Skwentna River basins
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains, including Moose Creek near Oilwell Road

Timing:

* Thursday evening through Saturday Evening. Heaviest rain Thursday
night through Friday morning.

Rainfall:

* Widespread rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain is likely (60-70%)
across the Susitna Valley late Thursday Night through Saturday
evening. Highest rain amounts will likely be in Susitna Valley
north of Talkeetna (including Petersville), and in Hatcher Pass.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Expect sharp rises on many small streams and rivers, including the
Yentna at Lake Creek. River rises from this upcoming Thursday
through Saturday storm will likely be less than was observed
following the Tuesday storm.

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 26 at 4:45PM MST until August 26 at 8:45PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...

* Until 845 PM MST.

* At 445 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Globe, Miami, Claypool, Central Heights-Midland City and
Inspiration.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 8:45 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 8:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.areaDesc: Arapahoe, CO; Douglas, CO; Elbert, CO
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 26 at 5:27PM MDT until August 26 at 8:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Elbert County in east central Colorado...
Southeastern Arapahoe County in northeastern Colorado...
Northeastern Douglas County in northeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 830 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 527 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Running Creek, Kiowa Creek, Bayou Gulch, Kinney Creek, Murphy
Creek, East Toll Gate Creek, Dry Creek, Happy Canyon Creek,
Newlin Gulch, Piney Creek, West Toll Gate Creek, Cherry Creek and
Coal Creek. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Southern Aurora, southeastern Centennial, Parker, The Pinery and
Foxfield.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 26 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Wednesday August 26 to 400 PM Thursday August 27

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Ozone concentrations in the Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups category are possible both Wednesday and Thursday
during the afternoon and evening hours. The best chance for these
elevated ozone levels will be in western parts of the Denver metro
area, including the adjacent foothills.  For Colorado air quality
conditions, forecasts, and advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Thursday, August 27, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone-pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion during the afternoons and evenings both
Wednesday and Thursday.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: El Paso, CO; Fremont, CO; Pueblo, CO
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 26 at 4:10PM MDT until August 26 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The 24 Burn Scar in...
East Central Fremont County in central Colorado...
Southwestern El Paso County in east central Colorado...
Northwestern Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 715 PM MDT.

* At 410 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the 24 Burn Scar. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.2 to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result
in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the 24 Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
24 Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Fremont, Southwestern El Paso
and Northwestern Pueblo Counties.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the 24 Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued August 26 at 1:33PM AKDT until August 28 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50
mph expected, mainly near the coast.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Western Capes, and Northern Bristol Bay
Coast.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 4 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong front will approach the Southwest
Alaska coastline by Thursday morning, bringing southerly to
southwesterly winds that are expected to gust to 50 mph, mainly for
coastal areas. The strongest winds look to push into Kuskokwim Bay
and across the Delta Thursday afternoon into the evening before
this corridor of winds shifts farther south and over Bristol Bay
Thursday night. With a long fetch of high end small craft and gale
force winds, this will result in higher waves and rough seas along
the Kuskokwim Bay coast. Even though winds are expected to slowly
decrease later Friday morning, high seas coinciding with high tide
Friday afternoon will likely push water levels 1 to 2 feet above
the normal high tide line for the Kuskokwim Bay coast.
properties.instruction: Secure outdoor objects.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 26 at 2:21PM PDT until August 28 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected through the work week,
with temperatures up to 115 to 118 across Death Valley and the
Colorado River Valley; up to 108 to 112 across Moapa Valley, the
Las Vegas Valley, the Pahrump Valley, and the Morongo Valley; up to
90 to 95 in the Hualapai Mountains. Overnight lows will be in the
upper-80s to low-90s for desert valleys.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/ Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and
loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued August 26 at 2:09PM PDT until August 28 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THROUGH 3 PM FRIDAY FOR MANY
INTERIOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHWEST CALIFORNIA DUE TO EXTREME HEAT AND
INSTABILITY ALONG WITH LOCALLY GUSTY WINDS AND LOW HUMIDITIES...

.A very hot and unstable air mass combined with locally gusty
winds and low humidities will bring a significant risk of large
plume dominated fires with rapid spread and extreme fire
behavior.

* TEMPERATURES...Highs 100 to 110 across the lower mountains,
adjacent foothills and the Cuyama Valley, and 85 to 95 across
higher mountains. Lows in the mid 70s to mid 80s common in the
mountains and foothills.

* INSTABILITY...Very deep mixing heights of 12,000 to 20,000
feet today through Thursday, slightly lower on Friday.

* WINDS...Local northwest to north winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts
up to 35 mph at times, strongest across the I-5 and Highway 33
corridors. A slightly stronger northerly wind push is possible
late Thursday night into Friday morning, with gusts up to 40
mph possible across the I-5 corridor.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimum humidities 10 to 20 percent each
day, with isolated values as low as 8 percent today and
Thursday. Poor recoveries overnight hours in the mountains and
foothills with humidities in the 15 to 30 percent range.

* IMPACTS...There is a significant risk of large plume dominated
fires with rapid fire spread and extreme fire behavior. There
is a history of large plume dominated fires this time of year
with similar weather and fuel conditions, including the
Bridge, Bobcat, and Station fires.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
will occur shortly. Use extreme caution with anything that can
spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland interfaces should be
prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks out. See
readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for information.

avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 26 at 11:54AM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air Quality
Advisory until noon PDT Friday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Advisory, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

For additional information...please visit the Web site at
http://www.oregon.gov/DEQ
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Kittitas, WA
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 26 at 11:54AM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology has issued an Air Quality
Alert until noon PDT Friday.

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Kittitas County through
Friday August 28 at noon due to current and expected wildfire smoke
from regional fires. Particulate matter (PM2.5) may reach Unhealthy
to Sensitive Groups to Unhealthy levels for areas directly downwind
from active fires, especially overnight and during the early morning
hours. Be sure to check air monitors in your area before outdoor
activities. When air quality is Unhealthy, everyone should reduce
exposure. Limit time outside, avoid, strenuous outdoor activity, and
follow tips for cleaner indoor air.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

drink plenty of water.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 26 at 11:20AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has extended
an Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area through
Thursday.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Medford has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from 2 PM to 8 PM PDT Thursday. The
Fire Weather Watch is no longer in effect.


* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In California...Fire weather zone 285. In
Oregon...the southern portions of Fire weather zones 624 and
625. This includes the Wrights Spring Fire in Klamath County.

* WIND...South to southwest at 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 30 to
40 mph both days. Winds trend higher Thursday.

* HUMIDITY...Daytime humidities down around 8 to 15 percent
both days.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
If you have not packed your go kit yet, now is the time to do so.
This includes items like important documents and essentials you
cannot live without. Fill your vehicle's fuel tank. Visit
ready.gov/kit for more information.


Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 26 at 6:47AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Snowfall will be likely through the day. Given the rain
beforehand and the near/above freezing temperatures, snow will
struggle to accumulate immediately but there will be minor
accumulations by this morning. There may be a brief break later
this morning into the early afternoon, likely allowing snow to
gradually melt. Then snow returns Wednesday evening before
diminishing into snow showers Thursday morning.

Additional snow totals around 1 to 2 inches are expected
early this morning in the area from Atigun Pass to Sagwon. Snow
will continue through the day but struggle to stick due to warmer
temperatures and higher sun angle. Another 1 to 2 inches of snow
are expected to accumulate tonight before tapering off.

properties.description:

daytime temperatures ranging from 95 to 100 degrees at Havasupai
Gardens, to 107 to 112 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 8 PM MST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

properties.areaDesc: Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 26 at 5:04PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern will continue to bring scattered to
numerous, locally heavy, showers and isolated to scattered
thunderstorms across portions of Yap State through Thursday night.
Frequent lightning, wind gusts to 25 knots, and choppy seas can be
expected with thunderstorms. Inter-island travel will be hazardous
through at least this Thursday night. Several inches of rain have
already fallen with this event, which is on top of the foot of rain
Yap saw last week. Due to saturated conditions, flash flooding and
mudslides are expected where the heaviest rain occurs. Residents
across Yap State should monitor local forecasts and heed advice of
emergency managers when heavy rainfall occurs.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAINFALL, FLASH FLOODING, MUDSLIDES, AND FREQUENT LIGHTNING TO CONTINUE THROUGH THURSDAY NIGHT ACROSS YAP STATE

properties.description:
Exposure to particle pollution can cause serious health problems;
aggravate lung disease, cause asthma attacks and acute bronchitis
and increase risk of respiratory infections. In people with heart
disease, short-term exposure to particle pollution has been linked
to heart attacks and arrhythmias according to the US
Environmental Protection Agency. Children and elderly people are
also more susceptible to consequences of high particulate levels.
Stay indoors if possible. Avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
physical activities to reduce the affect of unhealthy air. For
current air quality go to fire.airnow.gov

properties.areaDesc: Maricopa, AZ
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 25 at 9:17AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has extended
an Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area through
Wednesday.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: OZONE HIGH POLLUTION ADVISORY FOR MARICOPA COUNTY INCLUDING THE PHOENIX METRO AREA THROUGH WEDNESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Eastern San Fernando Valley; Eastern San Gabriel Mountains; Interstate 5 Corridor; Los Angeles County Inland Coast including Downtown Los Angeles; Los Angeles County San Gabriel Valley; Santa Clarita Valley; Santa Susana Mountains; Western San Fernando Valley; Western San Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 25 at 7:55AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the the South Coast Air Basin and Coachella Valley.
Levels of ozone pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...from 1 PM Monday to 8 PM Friday. The highest ozone levels
typically occur in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 24 at 1:34PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the the South Coast Air Basin and Coachella Valley.
Levels of ozone pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...from 1 PM Monday to 8 PM Friday. The highest ozone levels
typically occur in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening

For the latest air quality forecasts and information, visit the
website at aqmd.gov.
